aegis/eligibility/EligibilityClaim.title: EligibilityClaim
aegis/eligibility/EligibilityClaim.description:
The withdraw redeemer. `spot` is the VAULT-resolved, already-fresh spot the
 barrier floor is priced against (shared by every barrier policy in a batch,
 matching pool.ak's one-resolution-per-tx). Ignored by pure-depeg entries.

aegis/eligibility/PolicyTerms.title: PolicyTerms
aegis/eligibility/PolicyTerms.description:
Per-policy terms the vault pins to each new policy output, then hands to the
 logic for the floor judgment. `oracle_nft` gates the Depeg branch to
 established-stablecoin feeds (pool.ak CRITICAL-1); barrier ignores it.

aegis/registry/RuleSet.title: RuleSet
aegis/registry/RuleSet.description:
The RuleSet the vault's UNDERWRITE arm reads, and the only field it takes is
 `logic_hash` (`pool_vault.ak:252`) — the sole governance-swappable pointer.

 `policy_hash` and `marker_policy` are custody roots, and under Invariant S
 (V82-IMMUTABLE-CORE §2) the vault gets them from its OWN compile parameters
 (`pool_vault.ak:75-76`), never from here: settlement must resolve a policy it
 already sold with no registry read, so a hostile or bricked registry can
 shape only business that does not exist yet. Rotating them would redirect
 future coverage to an attacker script or strand every outstanding policy
 (#363 red-team H1-H4), which is why they were pinned even when the vault did
 read them.

 The two fields still have consumers, none of them a vault arm: `ruleset_eq`
 compares them, `check_propose` (:160-161) and `check_enact` (:190-191) pin
 them unchanged across every transition, and `offchain/scripts/v8_genesis.py`
 writes the derived hashes into the epoch-0 datum. Post-Invariant-S those
 pins are belt-and-braces — the vault's compile params are what actually bind
 custody — and the fields carry no authority a settlement path can reach.
 Everything else (oracle trust root, mandate, resolver hash, value movement)
 is vault-baked and NOT here by design.

fields.title: logic_hash
fields.description: eligibility-rules withdraw-0 validator (barrier/depeg dispatch + floors) — SWAPPABLE

fields.title: policy_hash
fields.description:
policy validator new policy outputs must land at. GENESIS-FIXED custody
 root, mirrored here; the vault binds it as a compile param, not from this.

fields.title: marker_policy
fields.description:
marker mint policy for policy outputs. GENESIS-FIXED custody root,
 mirrored here; the vault binds it as a compile param, not from this.

fields.title: utilisation_bps
fields.description:
share of the post-trade pool that may sit as live coverage, in bps. NAMED
 and rail-checked, but READ BY NO VALIDATOR: the book cap Underwrite
 enforces is the literal `nc * 3` in `vault.underwrite_ok`. Same hazard as
 `Floors` — the enactment that moves this must be the one that reads it.

fields.title: max_coverage_ratio
fields.description:
premium adequacy: coverage <= premium * this. CARRIED, not yet read —
 `is_premium_adequate` uses the compiled ratio.

fields.title: take_bps
fields.description:
the protocol's take of each premium, in bps — the RATE, bounded by
 `max_fee_take_rail_bps`. `treasury_bps` is treasury's share OF this take,
 not of the premium.

aegis/registry_v2/Floors.title: Floors
aegis/registry_v2/Floors.description:
The five baseline floors under the actuarial curve. Every value is basis
 points on the shared 10_000 scale, so the depeg band and the peg-health gate
 cannot drift onto two different divisors the way the percent forms in
 `floor_table` can.

 CARRIED AND RAIL-CHECKED, READ BY NO VALIDATOR. The floors Underwrite
 actually enforces are the compiled constants in `floor_table.ak`, reached
 through `vault.underwrite_baseline_ok`. Enacting a value here changes
 nothing today. That is a hazard rather than a nicety: the slice that
 de-constantises `underwrite_baseline_ok` makes every value silently enacted
 in the interim go live at once, with no further governance action — so the
 enactment that MOVES these must be the one that reads them.

fields.description: Some = governance handover (the team-multisig -> cMATRA rail)

fields.description: POSIX ms; EnactUpdate requires tx.lower >= this

aegis/registry_v2/UnderwriteConfig.title: UnderwriteConfig
aegis/registry_v2/UnderwriteConfig.description:
Everything Underwrite needs and settlement must never re-read. Values under
 `settlement_pins` are GOVERNED *sources*: Underwrite copies them into each
 new PolicyDatum, after which the policy is self-contained.

fields.title: mandates
fields.description:
primary AegisSelf NFT ↔ optional Pyth Lazer fallback (#"" = none). READ by
 Underwrite.

fields.title: publisher_vkh
fields.description:
AegisSelf feed-host VKH new policies pin. CARRIED, not yet read by any
 validator — width-bounded here and inert until one does.

fields.title: observer_hash
fields.description:
MIRROR of pool_vault's CORE `observer_script_hash`, not a governed value.
 `attested_price` reads the Price out of the redeemer of `Script(h)`, so the
 identity of this hash IS the reading's genuineness; governing it made the
 Underwrite spot buyer-authored (G10 red-team CRITICAL). Underwrite binds it
 EQUAL to its compile parameter, and only a SHAPE bound lives here, because
 the equality needs a hash this module must never learn.

fields.title: admissible_providers
fields.description:
providers Underwrite may sell against. A SET rail bounds it to the
 push-oracle predicate, so governance may ADD a provider but never one
 whose spot the buyer authors. Empty halts new business, like `mandates`.

fields.title: second_leg
fields.description:
[#403 FIX 1] WHICH pairs carry which second leg is GOVERNED and therefore
 reversible; the `min` MECHANISM that consumes it is compile-time and is
 the one-way door. That split is the whole shape of the decision: the
 mechanism ships at genesis because it is cheap and irreversible-later,
 the Pyth leg is armed per-pair afterwards without a migration.

fields.title: extension
fields.description:
[#390 / #403 FIX 5] RESERVED. One trailing slot, decoded by index and
 defaulted to `None`, so the next thing a policy has to carry does not cost
 a vault generation.

 It is ONE slot rather than two named fields on purpose. Two claimants are
 already known — ORACLE-ZERO E9's freeze-attestation hash (32 bytes, sizing
 answered) and a SHORT sale-side trailing low distinct from the 12h
 claim-side one — and inventing a second slot for the second claimant is
 how a datum acquires four half-used tails. They coordinate here.

 WHY THE SALE-SIDE LOW IS RESERVED AND NOT BUILT: one field cannot serve
 both sides. The sale gate wants a SHORT memory, because a 12-hour low
 makes cover unbuyable for twelve hours after a dip; the claim trigger
 wants a LONG one, because a 15-minute memory denies an honest claimant
 whose break happened an hour into a 7-day policy and recovered. Splitting
 them is a real design question with a real cost on either side, and it is
 not this generation's work — but the ROOM for it has to exist at genesis
 or the split becomes a migration.

 THE CONSTRAINT THIS SLOT INHERITS (see the module header): an
 already-deployed vault IGNORES a tail it does not know, so anything placed
 here can only ever WIDEN what a policy permits. A restriction written into
 the extension is invisible to exactly the vaults that would have to
 enforce it.

aegis/types/ReceiptWitness.title: ReceiptWitness
aegis/types/ReceiptWitness.description:
The revealed preimage of a policy's `receipt_commitment`. The
 `ClaimWithReceipt` path recomputes the commitment from these fields and
 requires it to equal `PolicyDatum.receipt_commitment`, so a committed policy
 names the exact Materios receipt + threshold it settles against, on-chain.

fields.title: receipt_id
fields.description: Materios receiptId (Bytes32, exactly 32 bytes).

fields.title: threshold
fields.description: The PUBLIC risk threshold (Uint64) proven by the Midnight circuit.

fields.title: config_hash
fields.description: Hash of the AI-cover config the proof was produced under (Bytes32, 32 bytes).

aegis/types/RiskClass.title: RiskClass
aegis/types/RiskClass.description:
Risk class of a policy — selects which on-chain premium-floor table the
 Underwrite branch dispatches to (and how the trigger is parameterized).

   * `Barrier` — one-touch down-and-in barrier on a *price* (ADA crash,
     Indigo CDP liquidation, Surf liquidation). Pays `coverage` if the
     underlying touches `strike = spot × (1 − d)` at any fresh oracle
     observation in `[start, expiry]`. Premium floor is strike-distance-,
     duration- and vol-aware (GBM first-passage at the conservative σ=85%
     grade), and Underwrite reads a fresh oracle reference input to derive
     the strike distance `d`.
   * `Depeg` — a stablecoin leaving its peg. The trigger strike is a fixed
     band below the peg (e.g. 0.95 × peg); the premium is hazard- (Poisson-)
     driven and duration-only, so Underwrite does NOT need a spot read for
     this class — only a strike-band sanity check.

 Set at Underwrite, immutable for the policy's life. Folding both classes
 into one datum lets a single pool-funded validator back every product line
 while charging each its correct actuarial floor.

aegis/types/SecondLeg.title: SecondLeg
aegis/types/SecondLeg.description:
[#403 FIX 1] THE SECOND, ONE-SIDED LEG the Underwrite gate feeds through
 `min`.

 `underwrite_baseline_ok` is MONOTONE NON-DECREASING in the resolved spot for
 both classes — Depeg's only spot conjunct is `depeg_peg_is_healthy(spot)`
 and Barrier's is `(spot - strike) * 10000 / spot >= min_strike_distance_bps`
 — so the buyer ALWAYS wants the print high. Feed any additional leg through
 `min` and his freedom to choose it is worth exactly zero: a lower number can
 only ever refuse him, and a stale leg causes a false DENIAL, never a false
 sale. That is what makes a BUYER-SUPPLIED pull attestation admissible here
 when it is inadmissible as the strike-setting primary.

 THE HONEST LIMIT, said out loud: `min` defends against selection among
 sources AT ONE INSTANT. It does NOT defend against correlated staleness — if
 the push leg is stale-high and the second leg is stale-high too, the
 composite is stale-high. The freshness that protects the pool is still
 carried by the PUSH leg's cadence.

anyOf.title: NoSecondLeg
anyOf.description:
No mandatory second leg: `min` degenerates to the primary print and the
 gate is exactly what it was. The reversible genesis posture for any pair
 whose second source is not yet provisioned.

anyOf.title: TrailingLowLeg
anyOf.description:
The SAME feed's key 3 `min_price_12h` — the publisher's own memory of the
 break the stale spot forgot. THE ASYMMETRY, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: for
 USDM / DJED / iUSD, where Pyth has no Lazer feed and never will, this leg
 is NOT source-independent. It defends against staleness and against a
 break the spot forgot; it does NOT defend against a compromised or wrong
 AegisSelf publisher. That is a difference in assurance level within one
 security model, not a second security model — and it is unavoidable: the
 zero-staleness alternative, a DEX reference input, is refuted by depth
 (DJED/ADA carries ~$206K, so faking peg health by 1% costs ~$514 of
 temporarily committed flow against a ~490 ADA edge per policy).

 Costs the vault NOTHING to arm: the validator already reads keys 3/4 and
 its `low_observed_at >= observed_at - trailing_low_window_ms` bound is a
 CEILING, so a shorter publisher window also satisfies it. On the 3-KEY
 shape every live depeg feed actually publishes, parsers default
 `min_price_12h` to spot, so `min` collapses to the spot gate and this leg
 is INERT — which is the graceful degradation, not a defect.

anyOf.title: PythPullLeg
anyOf.description:
A buyer-supplied Pyth Lazer pull attestation on `feed_id` — a genuinely
 independent source with its own signers (USDC / USDT / ADA). MANDATORY:
 an absent or stale leg REFUSES the sale rather than falling back to the
 primary alone, because a leg that can be omitted is not a leg.

 `require_confidence` is a CONJUNCT on this leg and never a closure: the
 buyer supplies the payload and therefore also supplies its confidence, so
 requiring it can only restrict him. It is per-mandate rather than the
 global `pyth_reject_absent_confidence` precisely because flipping that
 flag globally BRICKS real payloads — Lazer subscribers choose the
 `properties` list and every vendored signed fixture carries no confidence.

aegis/types/SettlementPins.title: SettlementPins
aegis/types/SettlementPins.description:
The GOVERNED values Underwrite copies into each new policy so settlement
 never reads mutable config (Invariant S). After the copy the policy is
 self-contained: a hostile registry can shape business that does not exist
 yet, never a policy that does. Class-shaped budgets are resolved to the
 policy's own class at Underwrite — pins carry concrete numbers, not tables.

fields.title: fallback_feed_id
fields.description:
Pyth Lazer feed id the fallback leg may settle against; empty = no
 fallback, primary attestation only.

fields.title: publisher_vkh
fields.description: DISCLOSED. Settlement checks the signer against CORE (`fallback.ak:56`).

fields.title: observer_script_hash
fields.description:
DISCLOSED. Settlement invokes the vault's COMPILE PARAMETER
 (`pool_vault.ak:114`, used at :458/:760/:891) — never this pin. A compile
 parameter is strictly more immutable than a pin, so the guarantee is
 stronger than the one this field appeared to make.

fields.title: max_reading_validity_ms
fields.description: DISCLOSED. `vault.ak:549-550` reads CORE `max_reading_validity_ms`.

fields.title: fallback_grace_ms
fields.description: DISCLOSED. The Pyth leg opens on CORE grace (`fallback.ak:223`).

fields.title: cancellation_window_ms
fields.description:
DISCLOSED. Cancel uses CORE `cancellation_window` (`pool_vault.ak:873`).
 [#420] Its governance rail is 24x `claim_waiting_period_ms`; the invariant
 `cancel_window_closes_before_any_policy_can_claim` binds the CONST, not
 this pin, so wiring a reader here needs the rail bound first.

fields.title: cancellation_fee_bps
fields.description: DISCLOSED. `pricing.ak:174-176` hardcodes the 10% and takes no fee argument.

fields.title: claim_waiting_period_ms
fields.description:
[#391 F1] Delay from `start_time` before this policy may be CLAIMED — a
 DISCLOSED term the buyer reads before paying, not a global constant that
 can move under him. Underwrite floors it at `claim_waiting_period_ms` for
 the policy's own class, so a pin may only ever be SAFER than CORE.

anyOf.title: AddLiquidity
anyOf.description: permissionless deposit; mints aLP pro-rata on the full pool total

anyOf.title: RemoveLiquidity
anyOf.description: atomic exit; burn the caller's own aLP, pay pro-rata of liquid backing

anyOf.title: DepositRevenue
anyOf.description: segregated first-loss/donation credit; no aLP minted

cardano/address/Address.title: Address
cardano/address/Address.description:
A Cardano `Address` typically holding one or two credential references.

 Note that legacy bootstrap addresses (a.k.a. 'Byron addresses') are
 completely excluded from Plutus contexts. Thus, from an on-chain
 perspective only exists addresses of type 00, 01, ..., 07 as detailed
 in [CIP-0019 :: Shelley Addresses](https://github.com/cardano-foundation/CIPs/tree/master/CIP-0019/#shelley-addresses).

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/PaymentCredential.title: PaymentCredential
cardano/address/PaymentCredential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/StakeCredential.title: StakeCredential
cardano/address/StakeCredential.description:
Represent a type of object that can be represented either inline (by hash)
 or via a reference (i.e. a pointer to an on-chain location).

 This is mainly use for capturing pointers to a stake credential
 registration certificate in the case of so-called pointer addresses.

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output
